title: Choose the repair that matches the failure
description: Select an observed incident, then choose an operator response. The result distinguishes client cache repair, keyspace maintenance, storage remediation, member replacement, and whole-cluster disaster recovery.

actions.label: Relist, record revision, resume watch
actions.detail: Rebuild the client cache from a current read and start the next watch from the returned revision.

actions.label: Delete, compact, defrag, then disarm
actions.detail: Remove unneeded keys, compact history, reclaim each member's file space, and clear NOSPACE only after evidence is healthy.

actions.label: Repair the durable storage path
actions.detail: Move or repair the slow WAL/backend device and verify fsync and backend commit latency under load.

actions.label: Replace one member through quorum
actions.detail: Remove and add one member at a time while the remaining voting majority stays healthy.

actions.label: Restore a tested snapshot as a new cluster
actions.detail: Create new member and cluster identity, then reconnect clients only after integrity and revision behavior are verified.

incidents.label: Watcher requests compacted history
incidents.detail: A controller reconnects from a revision older than the retained MVCC history.
evidence: The server reports the requested watch revision has been compacted.
A current range read succeeds and returns a newer response revision.
The client cache can be rebuilt from authoritative key-value state.
requiredSequence: Discard the incomplete local cache rather than guessing missed events.
Perform the required current range read and record its response revision.
Resume the watch after that revision and handle another compaction race.

relist-watch.headline: The client re-establishes a complete state boundary.
relist-watch.consequence: A fresh list plus revision closes the gap that compacted watch history can no longer replay.

recover-space.headline: More maintenance cannot recreate deleted event history.
recover-space.consequence: Compaction is the reason the old events are unavailable. Defragmentation changes file allocation, not client cache correctness.

fix-storage.headline: Storage replacement does not repair a stale cache.
fix-storage.consequence: The cluster is serving current data; the watcher must rebuild from a current revision.

replace-member.headline: Member replacement targets the wrong boundary.
replace-member.consequence: Every healthy member observes the same compacted history window. Replacing one member does not restore old watch events.

restore-cluster.headline: A cluster restore is disproportionate and risks regression.
restore-cluster.consequence: The authoritative cluster is healthy. Restoring an older snapshot can lose newer committed state and invalidate more watchers.

incidents.label: Backend quota raises NOSPACE
incidents.detail: The cluster enters limited-operation maintenance mode after backend usage reaches its configured quota.
evidence: The alarm list contains NOSPACE and endpoint status shows high backend use.
Live keyspace size and retained revision history are both measured.
A reviewed set of keys or old history can be removed safely.
requiredSequence: Delete unnecessary live keys and stop the workload causing unbounded growth.
Compact old MVCC revisions so etcd can reuse their pages.
Defragment members one at a time to return free pages to the filesystem.
Verify space and health, then disarm NOSPACE and test a bounded write.

relist-watch.headline: Refreshing a watcher does not free backend space.
relist-watch.consequence: The cluster remains in maintenance mode because key and history storage still exceed the quota.

recover-space.headline: The response addresses logical history and physical file space.
recover-space.consequence: Compaction makes old revisions reusable; defragmentation returns that reusable space to the filesystem. The alarm is cleared only after verification.

fix-storage.headline: A larger or faster disk buys time but leaves growth unbounded.
fix-storage.consequence: The current quota and retained history still need correction, or the replacement storage will fill again.

replace-member.headline: Replacing a member does not remove cluster-wide key history.
replace-member.consequence: The restored member catches up to the same oversized logical state and the NOSPACE condition remains.

restore-cluster.headline: Snapshot restore is not routine space maintenance.
restore-cluster.consequence: It can discard committed changes and creates an avoidable cluster-identity migration while the existing quorum is healthy.

incidents.label: WAL fsync latency spikes
incidents.detail: Write latency and leader stability degrade while disk persistence histograms rise.
evidence: WAL fsync or backend commit latency rises on one or more members.
Peer RTT, CPU throttling, and application request shape are checked separately.
Pending proposals or leader changes correlate with the storage slowdown.
requiredSequence: Protect the workload with admission control and preserve a voting majority.
Repair or replace the slow durable storage path one member at a time.
Re-run a representative benchmark and verify proposal and leadership metrics.

relist-watch.headline: Client cache refresh does not shorten durable commits.
relist-watch.consequence: Writes still wait on the slow consensus storage path and the cluster can remain unstable.

recover-space.headline: Maintenance helps only if fragmentation is the measured cause.
recover-space.consequence: Live defragmentation blocks a member and can worsen latency. Do not use it as a generic fix for slow fsync.

fix-storage.headline: The response repairs the physical commit bottleneck.
fix-storage.consequence: Healthy low-latency durable storage reduces the RTT-plus-fsync floor that constrains Raft commits.

replace-member.headline: Replacement works only when it includes a healthy storage path.
replace-member.consequence: Replacing a member on the same overloaded device or class reproduces the failure.

restore-cluster.headline: Restoring data does not make the storage device faster.
restore-cluster.consequence: The new cluster can inherit the same latency fault while adding unnecessary recovery risk.

incidents.label: One member reports corruption
incidents.detail: A healthy voting majority remains available while one member's persisted state diverges.
evidence: Endpoint and hash checks isolate the problem to one member.
The remaining voting members still form a healthy majority.
A current snapshot and the affected data directory are preserved for analysis.
requiredSequence: Stop or isolate the affected member without removing another voter.
Use the version-matched corruption runbook to purge or replace that member.
Wait for catch-up, verify hashes and health, then clear the alarm.

relist-watch.headline: A client relist does not repair persisted member state.
relist-watch.consequence: The corrupt replica remains unsafe even if a client happens to read from a healthy member.

recover-space.headline: Compaction and defrag are not corruption repair.
recover-space.consequence: Changing storage layout can destroy evidence without restoring agreement.

fix-storage.headline: Hardware repair may prevent recurrence but does not rebuild state.
fix-storage.consequence: The member still needs a documented purge or replacement path from healthy cluster data.

replace-member.headline: The healthy quorum can safely rebuild one replica.
replace-member.consequence: One-at-a-time replacement preserves quorum and lets the new member catch up from authoritative state.

restore-cluster.headline: Whole-cluster restore expands the blast radius.
restore-cluster.consequence: A healthy majority already contains authoritative state. Restoring every member risks losing newer commits.

incidents.label: Voting majority is permanently lost
incidents.detail: Too few original voters can form quorum and the missing members cannot be recovered.
evidence: The original voting majority cannot be restored safely.
The latest usable snapshot has a known revision, integrity result, and protected copy.
RPO, cluster endpoints, certificates, and dependent-client restart behavior are approved.
requiredSequence: Fence every surviving old member and preserve forensic evidence.
Restore the tested snapshot into new member directories and a new cluster identity.
For revision-sensitive consumers, apply the version-supported revision bump and mark-compacted procedure.
Verify hashes, alarms, membership, TLS, and application reconciliation before reopening writes.

relist-watch.headline: Clients cannot relist from a cluster without quorum.
relist-watch.consequence: The authoritative service cannot prove a current read or commit a write.

recover-space.headline: Space maintenance cannot recreate a voting majority.
recover-space.consequence: Compaction and defragmentation operate on storage, not lost consensus membership.

fix-storage.headline: Repair surviving disks only helps if the old majority returns.
fix-storage.consequence: When missing voters are permanently lost, durable storage on a minority cannot authorize new commits.

replace-member.headline: Runtime membership changes require the quorum that is gone.
replace-member.consequence: Adding or removing members through the unavailable cluster cannot safely establish a new authority.

restore-cluster.headline: A tested snapshot becomes the recovery authority.
restore-cluster.consequence: Restore creates new cluster and member identity. Clients must reconcile the declared RPO and invalidate revision-sensitive caches correctly.
